- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a “cool-down” correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Model shows persistent bias toward higher prices in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply downward bias correction for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- If sentiment turns positive after a prolonged negative streak, model often fails to capture the momentum; increase forecast by 1–2% for 2–4 days following sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is evident when model forecasts stay above 3–5% above recent 7-day average; reduce forecast by 1–2% for 3–5 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate when sentiment is mixed or trending downward; apply a 1–3% downward adjustment if sentiment is ≤0.33 over last 5 days.
